findings.summary: row is read from mcp_budget.VIEW_BUDGETS[("roadmap", "brief")] and line 371 then asserts mcp_budget.view_budget("roadmap", {}) == row, so both sides of the assertion resolve from the same table and a row lowered back to the summary's 20,000 moves them together and passes. The companion size check at line 375 cannot compensate: the fixture's brief measures 6,967 characters against the 30,000 row (and would also pass the pre-fix 20,000 row), against reckon's own 17,772, so neither added assertion reddens on the defect this commit repairs unless DEFAULT_VIEWS is reverted as well.

The big_project fixture (40 plans chained linearly, 10 sections each, helper at line 287) re-implements the synthetic mounted-project capability already owned by tests/test_every_default_read_fits.py:107 (PLANS=60, SECTIONS=400, whose sweep at line 294 covers roadmap view="brief" after this commit's ROADMAP_VIEWS change) rather than extending it. It also fails the commit body's claim: because 39 of the 40 plans are blocked the brief carries 7 lines and one ready row and serialises to 6,967 characters, so 'a brief that repeated every section would fail here' does not hold for this fixture.

The new comment pins 'On this repository's own project that is 17,772 characters, 1,963 of them prose' — a measurement of the mounted project at the time of writing that drifts as plans land, so a later reader choosing this row reads a stale figure as the basis for the 30,000 ceiling; a snapshot of a moving number is the fuse the repository's own test rules warn about.
